title: Key two lock plugs alike: every key pin flush with the shear line
instruction: Key both lock plugs alike to the code 3-1-4-2, chamber 1 being the one nearest the key's bow. Into each chamber drop one key pin of the size its code number gives, taken from the pin kit (size 1, the shortest, is in the kit's nearest row; size 5, the longest, is in its farthest), so that every pin stands on the key and ends flush with the top of its plug, with nothing else in or over the chamber.
context: Rekeying pin-tumbler cylinders is the most common locksmith job (new owners, lost keys, tenant changes; O*NET 49-9094.00 Locksmiths and Safe Repairers). A common request is front and back doors keyed alike, so one key opens both. With the new key in each plug, the locksmith drops into every chamber the key pin whose size number matches the key's cut there, then checks that every key pin top is flush with the plug's surface, the shear line. A pin one step proud or low stops the plug from turning. As a robot task it is choosing parts by a numeric code and setting each one precisely into a narrow chamber, eight times over two cylinders, the arms taking turns at one shared pin kit. The check needs no code sheet: a straightedge across each plug shows every wrong pin 4.6 mm or more proud or low (6 mm when upright), so the task is producing a measured coplanar surface, not following a lookup rule.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, heights are above the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Everything is fixed to the table except the ten key pins; every fixed part is a box, and boxes meet face to face with no overlap. (1) Left plug: a grey aluminium training plug, an enlarged model of a pin-tumbler lock plug taken out of its shell, 186 mm along x (x 20.7 to 39.3 cm), 50 mm wide (y 21.5 to 26.5 cm, centred y +24.0 cm) and 60 mm tall, with four open-topped square chambers 34 x 34 mm in a row along x, centred at x 23.4, 27.8, 32.2 and 36.6 cm (chamber 1 nearest the robot). It is built from two side walls 186 x 8 x 60 mm centred at x 30.0 cm, y +21.9 and +26.1 cm, and five cross walls 10 (x) x 34 (y) x 60 mm centred at y +24.0 cm and x 21.2, 25.6, 30.0, 34.4 and 38.8 cm (end walls, and 10 mm walls between the chambers). (2) Left key: light silver nickel-silver blocks. Each chamber's floor is a 34 x 34 mm block standing for the new key's cut under that chamber, 20, 32, 14 and 26 mm tall in chambers 1 to 4, so the chambers are 40, 28, 46 and 34 mm deep. The key's bow, a block 12 (x) x 30 (y) x 30 mm (tall) centred at x 20.1 cm, y +24.0 cm, touches the plug's near end and shows that the key is in. (3) Right plug and key: identical, mirrored to y -24.0 cm (side walls at y -21.9 and -26.1 cm, bow at x 20.1 cm, y -24.0 cm). (4) Pin kit: a floorless grey plastic pinning-kit tray standing on the table, x 10.5 to 33.9 cm, y -6.2 to +6.2 cm, with walls 4 mm thick and 6 mm tall forming ten open cells 42 (x) x 56 (y) mm inside, in 5 rows along x (row centres x 13.0, 17.6, 22.2, 26.8 and 31.4 cm, row 1 nearest the robot) and 2 columns (centres y +3.0 and -3.0 cm): three 234 mm walls along x centred at x 22.2 cm, y 0 and +-6.0 cm, and twelve 56 mm segments across y at x 10.7, 15.3, 19.9, 24.5, 29.1 and 33.7 cm, one in each column. (5) Ten key pins, loose: gold-anodised aluminium cylinders 24 mm across, standing upright on the table at the cell centres; row n of each column holds one size-n pin. Size 1: 28 mm long, 34 g; size 2: 34 mm, 41 g; size 3: 40 mm, 49 g; size 4: 46 mm, 56 g; size 5: 52 mm, 64 g. Sizes 1 to 4 are each needed twice (once per plug); the two size-5 pins are spares. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored every control step from the pins' poses and the two grippers' tool points (TCP: the point 13 mm above the finger tips). A chamber is pinned when all five hold: (a) a key pin stands in it: the pin's centre, seen from above, is inside the chamber's 34 x 34 mm opening, and its axis is at most 8 degrees from vertical (either end up); (b) the centre of its top face is within 2.5 mm of the plug's top surface (the shear line), above or below; (c) it is still: its centre's path over the last 0.5 s is under 2 mm; (d) it is let go: neither gripper's TCP is within 50 mm of its top-face centre (at a step when the grippers cannot be read, no chamber counts as let go); (e) nothing else is over it: no part of any other pin, seen from above at any height, lies over that chamber's opening (a second pin stacked on it or beside it in the chamber, standing or lying on the plug's top across the opening, or held above it). k is the number of pinned chambers over both plugs (0 to 8), and the score is k/8. Possible scores: 0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.625, 0.75, 0.875 and 1.0. Success (1.0) is k = 8, both cylinders keyed alike to 3-1-4-2; the trial ends early once k = 8 has held for 1 s, and otherwise the last step is scored by the same rule. A chamber left empty, holding a wrong pin or two pins, with its pin still held or moving, or with anything over it simply does not count; pins in the kit, on the table or on a plug top away from every chamber opening neither add nor subtract. Only the code's pin can count: sizes differ by 6 mm, so a pin one size off stands 6 mm proud or sits 6 mm low; two pins stacked stand at least 10 mm proud; only size 1 fits lying in a chamber with clearance (size 2 is exactly 34 mm), and the 8 degree rule rejects either; the 34 mm chamber caps any lean at 13 to 27 degrees, so no standing pin can fall flat in it; a pin left leaning more than 8 degrees (for example with its foot caught against a chamber wall) does not count; at 8 degrees or less its top moves by at most 1.4 mm, so a correct pin still reads flush and a wrong one stays 4.6 mm or more off. In a real trial, lay a straightedge across the plug top over each chamber: the pin is flush if a 2.5 mm feeler gauge does not pass between the straightedge and the pin top and the pin does not lift the straightedge 2.5 mm or more. Tilt is judged against a square; stillness, let-go and anything over a chamber from the video's last second and a top photo.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, one friction. An enlarged training model, not to one scale: pins about 7x real length (28-52 mm against 4-8 mm), size steps 16x (6 mm against 0.38 mm), so the 2.5 mm flush tolerance still separates sizes. The plug is a fixed block with square chambers; the key is fixed and shown only by its cut depths (the floor blocks); shell, driver pins and springs are not modelled, so flushness stands in for 'the plug turns'. Pins are light aluminium.
reset_notes: Stand each pin back upright at the centre of its kit cell, row n = size n (size 1 in the row nearest the robot), in both columns. Everything else is fixed; nothing is consumed.
